blocks.content: FCI's open-ended procurement policy without adequate storage facilities has resulted in severe operational inefficiencies and mounting food subsidies.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Open-ended procurement of wheat and paddy leads to buffer stocks far exceeding prescribed norms, straining fiscal resources.
Inadequate modern silo capacity forces reliance on Cover and Plinth (CAP) storage, causing significant grain degradation and spoilage.
High economic cost of foodgrains stems from rising MSPs, statutory state levies, labor charges, and inefficient handling costs.
Geographical concentration of procurement in traditional surplus states like Punjab and Haryana leaves other regional farmers under-served.
The Shanta Kumar Committee recommended outsourcing procurement to states with stable infrastructure and transitioning to direct benefit transfers (DBT).

items: Components of FCI's Economic Cost (MSP + Procurement Incidentals + Distribution Costs) are frequently tested in Prelims and Mains.
Key recommendations of the Shanta Kumar Committee (2015) on restructuring FCI form a recurring theme in UPSC Mains GS-III.
Differentiate clearly between physical buffer stock requirements and economic carrying costs in food security questions.
